positions.name: NVIDIA Corp.
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS BEAT GAPPER - THE CATALYST THAT SET THE WHOLE TAPE: NVIDIA reported FQ2 after the 8/26 close at $96.2B revenue vs a $92.27B consensus and $2.22 EPS vs $2.09, with Data Center at $89.0B vs $85.4B expected. It then guided FQ3 to $108B +/- 2% against a $104.2B street number - and explicitly excluded ALL China data-center sales from that guide. Huang additionally forecast ~70% fiscal-2028 revenue growth, far above estimates. NVDA is +6.58% pre-market at 223.45 on a 223.30/223.46 book - a one-cent spread on the most liquid stock in the market.
positions.risks: GROSS MARGIN IS THE ONE SOFT SPOT: FQ3 gross margin was guided to 74%, down from 75%, which is what capped the initial after-hours pop. At 223.45 the stock is only 5.5% below its 236.54 52-week high set 5/14, so we are buying strength, not a discount - 32.6x earnings and 26.4x book on a $5.16T market cap. A gap of this size on this much market cap tends to see profit-taking into the first hour. Overnight only.

positions.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 8/31 or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 READ-THROUGH - HBM IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON NVDA'S $108B GUIDE: Micron supplies the high-bandwidth memory that goes into every Blackwell/Rubin rack, so an $89B Data Center quarter guided to accelerate is a direct volume signal for MU's CMBU segment. MU is +4.26% pre-market at 978.36 on a 978.50/979.00 book - a 50-cent spread on a $1.06T name. At 21.1x earnings it is the cheapest large-cap in the AI complex and it has no earnings event until late September, so the swing window is clean of company-specific risk.
positions.risks: MU IS UP ~8.5x OFF ITS 114.25 52-WEEK LOW (set 9/2/2025) AND IS THE MOST VIOLENT CHART IN THE BOOK - it is also 22% below its 1255.00 high from 6/25, meaning it has already had one 20%+ drawdown inside this uptrend. Memory is a cyclical business being priced as a secular one; a single hyperscaler capex headline can take 10% out of it in a session. The 3-share size is forced by the $3,500 cap and the ~$978 share price, so this is the coarsest position in the book - one share is 33% of the risk. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Coherent Corp.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 8/31 or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 READ-THROUGH VIA OPTICAL INTERCONNECT: Coherent's Networking segment builds the 800G/1.6T transceivers and optical engines that scale out GPU clusters, so NVDA's $108B guide reads straight into its datacom order book. COHR is +4.51% pre-market at 307.64 on a 307.80/307.86 book - a six-cent spread, the tightest quote in the entire new book. It sits 30% below its 440.00 high from 6/3, so this is a base breaking out rather than an extended chart being chased.
positions.risks: 71.4x TRAILING EARNINGS ON A BUSINESS WITH TWO NON-AI SEGMENTS (Materials and Lasers) THAT ARE NOT GROWING AT ANYTHING LIKE THE DATACOM RATE - the multiple is being paid for roughly half the company. COHR has run from 85.94 (9/2/2025) to 440.00 and back to 307.64 in twelve months, a 3.6x round trip that tells you how fast this name de-rates when the AI bid pauses. Transceiver pricing is also under structural pressure from Chinese competition. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Vertiv Holdings Co.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 8/31 or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 READ-THROUGH VIA DATA-CENTER POWER AND COOLING: Vertiv sells the busbar, switchgear and liquid-cooling infrastructure that every Blackwell rack requires, and its own raised FY26 guide (organic net sales growth of 30-32%, adjusted diluted EPS $6.65-6.75, adjusted FCF $2.4-2.6B) is now being validated by NVDA's $108B quarter. VRT is +4.39% pre-market at 275.39 on a 274.73/275.51 book. It is 27.5% below its 379.94 high from 5/14.
positions.risks: THE GUIDANCE RAISE ITSELF IS NOT FRESH NEWS - it came with Q2 in late July, so what we are actually buying today is the NVDA read-through, not a same-day Vertiv catalyst. That is a weaker basis than a company-specific print. 57.9x earnings and 20.7x book on a $101B name whose revenue is concentrated in a handful of hyperscaler customers with real order lumpiness. VRT has historically gapped 10%+ in BOTH directions on capex headlines. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 8/31 or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 READ-THROUGH WITH THE STRONGEST CONFIRMING MOVE IN THE COMPLEX: Credo's active electrical cables and SerDes chiplets are the copper interconnect inside AI racks, and it is +5.97% pre-market at 240.00 - the largest gain of any NVDA derivative this morning and nearly matching NVDA's own +6.6%. The book is 238.92/240.20. It is 22% below its 308.67 high from 6/22.
positions.risks: 90.3x EARNINGS AND 20.4x BOOK ON A $42B COMPANY WITH 807 EMPLOYEES AND EXTREME CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION - a majority of Credo's revenue has historically come from a very small number of hyperscalers, so a single design-loss headline is an existential-scale move for this stock, not a 5% one. It has gone from 86.49 (3/30/2026) to 308.67 to 240.00 in five months. This is the highest-beta name in today's book and the +5.97% pre-market gain means we are paying for the read-through rather than anticipating it. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Royal Bank of Canada
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS BEAT THIS MORNING: RBC reported fiscal Q3 before the open at 3.07 vs a 2.89 estimate on the verified calendar - a 6.2% surprise. It is +1.35% pre-market at 210.00 and is now within 4% of its 218.57 52-week high set 7/16. This is the second consecutive quarter of clean Canadian bank beats and the group is being repriced as a whole.
positions.risks: THE US PRE-MARKET BOOK IS 204.90/213.71 - A 4.2% SPREAD ON A CROSS-LISTED NAME - so the 210.00 entry rests on a single 06:54 ET print rather than a two-sided market. That is the standing problem with trading Canadian banks off the US tape. RY has run from 141.37 (8/27/2025) to 218.57 in twelve months, so 49% of the re-rating is already done at 18.5x earnings and 3.0x book. Canadian credit provisions remain the swing factor and management commentary on the call can undo a 6% EPS beat in one sentence. Overnight only.

positions.name: The Toronto-Dominion Bank
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS BEAT - THE LARGEST SURPRISE OF THE CANADIAN BANK GROUP: TD reported fiscal Q3 before the open at 1.98 vs a 1.74 estimate (verified) - a 13.8% surprise, more than double RY's. It is +1.11% pre-market at 120.75 with the bid AT 120.75, i.e. the print is being supported rather than faded, and the stock is 3.8% below its 125.47 high from 8/17.
positions.risks: THE ASK IS 123.50 AGAINST A 120.75 BID - A 2.3% SPREAD - so this entry is marked at the bid-side print, and a real fill would likely be worse. TD has nearly doubled from 72.73 (8/28/2025) in twelve months, the fastest move of any major North American bank, which means the anti-money-laundering remediation overhang that suppressed the stock has already been fully unwound as a story. At 19.3x earnings TD is now the most expensive of the three Canadian banks in this book on a P/E basis despite the biggest beat. Overnight only.

CM is also the smallest and most domestically-concentrated of the three, so a Canadian housing or consumer-credit headline hits it hardest. Overnight only.

positions.name: Vistra Corp.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 8/31 or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 2 AI-POWER READ-THROUGH FROM THE BOTTOM OF A BASE: NVDA guiding to $108B of quarterly revenue is a direct statement about how much electricity the AI buildout will consume, and Vistra's ERCOT and PJM nuclear/gas fleet is the merchant generator most levered to that demand. VST is +2.19% pre-market at 143.10 on a 143.15/143.23 book - an eight-cent spread. Critically, it is only 7.9% above its 132.66 52-week LOW set 5/19 and 35% below its 219.82 high, so unlike the semis this is a washed-out chart, not an extended one.
positions.risks: THE REASON IT IS NEAR ITS LOW IS THAT THE AI-POWER TRADE HAS ALREADY BEEN TRIED AND FAILED ONCE - VST peaked at 219.82 on 9/22/2025 and has spent eleven months de-rating as data-center power-purchase agreements arrived slower and at worse terms than the 2024 narrative implied. Buying the read-through again requires believing this time is different. 23.5x earnings but 15.5x book on a capital-intensive utility. Merchant power is also exposed to natural gas prices and ERCOT weather, neither of which has anything to do with NVDA. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Constellation Energy Corp.

CEG is +1.20% pre-market at 282.88 on a 281.41/282.87 book. It is 23.7% below its 412.70 high from 10/15/2025 and 23.7% above its 228.63 low from 7/1 - roughly mid-range, which is the most neutral entry in today's book.
positions.risks: THE +1.20% PRE-MARKET MOVE IS THE WEAKEST CONFIRMATION OF ANY NEW POSITION TODAY - the market is not treating CEG as an NVDA derivative this morning the way it is treating CRDO or COHR, so this is a thesis trade rather than a momentum trade. Same failed-narrative history as VST: the nuclear-PPA story peaked in October 2025 and has de-rated since. 27.1x earnings. Regulatory risk around behind-the-meter data-center interconnects at nuclear plants remains genuinely unresolved at FERC. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: Dollar General Corp.
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 EARNINGS BEAT GAPPER - THE BIGGEST NON-AI MOVE ON THE TAPE: Dollar General reported Q2 before the open at 2.48 vs a 1.99 estimate (verified) - a 24.6% surprise - and the stock is +9.14% pre-market at 134.00 on a 134.00/135.75 book with the bid AT 134.00. This is the trade-down consumer thesis working: DG benefits from exactly the household stress that produced the DKS and KSS misses. It cleared its 158.23 high from 2/26 by only 15% to the upside remaining, and 8/26 volume of 3.24M ran 59% above its 2.04M average into the print.
positions.risks: WE JUST CLOSED THIS POSITION THIS MORNING FOR A +322 GAIN AND ARE IMMEDIATELY RE-ENTERING 9% HIGHER - that is buying our own winner after the gap, which is a materially worse risk/reward than the pre-earnings entry was. Dollar General has a long, well-documented history of walking back strong Q2 prints on the guidance portion of the call, and the call happens after this entry. A +9% gap on a $27B retailer also invites same-day fading. Overnight only, and the size is at the cap so there is no room to average.
